facts.fact: The Ito-toren is a 100-metre office building in the Zuidas district of Amsterdam.
facts.quote: The Ito-toren (Dutch for Ito Tower) is a 100 metres (328 feet) tall office building in the Zuidas in the Dutch capital city Amsterdam.

facts.fact: It was built between September 2002 and June 2005 as part of the first phase of the Mahler4 complex.
facts.quote: The construction of the Ito-toren was part of the first construction phase of Mahler4 and took place between September 2002 and June 2005.

facts.fact: Toyo Ito and his firm designed it, and the tower is named after him; ZZDP Architecten was also involved in the design.
facts.quote: Toyo Ito, after whom the building is named, and his architecture firm designed the office building. ZZDP Architecten was involved in the design process as well.

facts.fact: It has 25 floors above ground and two below.
facts.quote: The Ito-toren has twenty-five above ground floors and two underground floors.

facts.fact: Its supporting elements are reinforced concrete, with a steel frame.
facts.quote: The supporting elements of the Ito-toren are made of reinforced concrete and the building has a steel frame.

facts.fact: The exterior is angular and pierced with holes, and the facade alternates horizontal bands of windows with bands of aluminium panels.
facts.quote: The Ito-toren has an angular exterior with holes in it. The facade is characterized by horizontal rows of windows with rows of aluminium panels in between them.

facts.fact: Inside there are four atria.
facts.quote: Inside the Ito-toren, there are four atria.

facts.fact: A large rooftop terrace sits on the 16th floor.
facts.quote: Besides, the Ito-toren has a large rooftop terrace on the 16th floor.

facts.fact: Torre Picasso is a Madrid skyscraper by Minoru Yamasaki; at 157 m and 43 floors it was the city's tallest building from 1988 to 2007.
facts.quote: Torre Picasso (Picasso Tower) is a skyscraper in Madrid, Spain designed by Minoru Yamasaki.  From 1988 until 2007 it was the tallest building in Madrid, measuring 515 ft (157 m) and with 43 floors.

facts.fact: It stands next to Pablo Picasso Square in the AZCA business complex on the Paseo de la Castellana.
facts.quote: Torre Picasso is located next to the Pablo Picasso Square, within the commercial complex AZCA along the Paseo de la Castellana.

facts.fact: In 1975 the developer gave the design to Yamasaki, working with Jorge Mir Valls and Rafael Coll Pujol.
facts.quote: Construction of this area, better known as AZCA, began in 1970 and in 1975 the developer Unión de Explosivos Río Tinto, S.A. awarded the design of the tower to American architect Minoru Yamasaki, in collaboration with Jorge Mir Valls and Rafael Coll Pujol.

facts.fact: Construction began in late 1982 and the tower opened in December 1988.
facts.quote: Construction began late 1982, and the building opened in December 1988.

facts.fact: The tower has a rectangular footprint on a windowless two-storey base, entered under a wide round arch that carries the facade above.
facts.quote: The structure has a rectangular footprint with a windowless two-storey base.  A wide round arch, resting on an underground steel structure for support, serves as the entrance and supports the façade above.

facts.fact: Windows on floors 3 to 43 are paired, divided by a slender pier.
facts.quote: Windows on floors 3 through 43 are grouped in twos divided by a slender pier.

facts.fact: The facade is clad in white aluminium and the corners are chamfered.
facts.quote: The façade is covered in white aluminum and the corners of the structure are chamfered.

facts.fact: The top two floors are windowless and the parapet flares out into a cornice.
facts.quote: The top two floors are also windowless and the parapet flares to form a cornice.

facts.fact: Mode Gakuen Spiral Towers is a 170-metre, 36-storey educational building in Nakamura-ku, Nagoya.
facts.quote: Mode Gakuen Spiral Towers (モード学園スパイラルタワーズ, Mōdo gakuen supairaru tawāzu) is a 170-metre (558 ft), 36-story educational facility located in Nakamura-ku, Nagoya, Aichi, Japan.

facts.fact: It houses three vocational schools: Nagoya Mode Gakuen, HAL Nagoya and Nagoya Isen.
facts.quote: The building is home to three vocational schools: Nagoya Mode Gakuen, HAL Nagoya and Nagoya Isen.

facts.fact: It is one of the tallest buildings in Nagoya.
facts.quote: It is one of the tallest buildings in Nagoya.

facts.fact: It was commissioned by Hürrem Sultan (Roxelana), wife of the Ottoman sultan Süleyman the Magnificent.
facts.quote: It was commissioned by Hürrem Sultan (also known as Roxelana), consort and wife of the Ottoman sultan Süleyman the Magnificent.

facts.fact: Mimar Sinan designed it on the site of the ancient Baths of Zeuxippus, for the religious community of the nearby Hagia Sophia.
facts.quote: It was designed by Mimar Sinan on the site of the historical Baths of Zeuxippus for the religious community of the nearby Hagia Sophia.

facts.fact: Sinan built the public bathhouse in 1556 as a charitable project.
facts.quote: The public bathhouse was constructed as a charitable project by architect Mimar Sinan in 1556.

facts.fact: The 75-metre building has two symmetrical sections, for men and women, set on one north–south axis, a novelty in Turkish bathhouse design.
facts.quote: The 75 m (246 ft) long structure is designed in the style of classical Ottoman baths, having two symmetrical separate sections for males and females. Both sections, situated in a north–south direction, are on the same axis that was a novelty in Turkish bathhouse architecture.

facts.fact: The outer walls alternate one course of cut stone with two courses of brick.
facts.quote: The exterior walls are built in courses of one cut stone and two bricks.

facts.fact: Each section has three linked rooms: a changing room, a cool room and a hot room.
facts.quote: Each section consists of three basic, interconnected rooms, namely the changing room (soyunmalık), the intermediate cool room (soğukluk, frigidarium) and the hot room (sıcaklık, caldarium).

facts.fact: The large dome of the hot room rests on octagonal walls and has small glass windows that let in a half-light from above.
facts.quote: The large dome of the hot room, which sits on the octagonal-shaped walls, has small glass windows to create a half-light from the top.

facts.fact: After a three-year restoration that began in 2008 and cost US$11 million, the bathhouse reopened in May 2011.
facts.quote: After a three-year-long restoration project that began in 2008 and cost US$11 million, the bathhouse reopened in May 2011.

facts.fact: Sinan built the Sinan Pasha Mosque at Beşiktaş between 1553 and 1555 for Grand Admiral Sinan Pasha, as a smaller version of the Üç Şerefeli Mosque in Edirne.
facts.quote: Between 1553 and 1555, Sinan built the Sinan Pasha Mosque at Beşiktaş, a smaller version of the Üç Şerefeli Mosque at Edirne, for the Grand Admiral Sinan Pasha.

facts.fact: Sinan reused its form in 1554 for Kara Ahmet Pasha's mosque, his first hexagonal mosque.
facts.quote: In 1554, Sinan used the form of the Sinan Pasha mosque again for the construction of the mosque for the next Grand Vizier Kara Ahmet Pasha in Constantinople, his first hexagonal mosque.

facts.fact: Victor Horta designed the Hôtel Solvay for Armand Solvay, son of the industrialist Ernest Solvay; it was built between 1895 and 1900 in the Art Nouveau style.
facts.quote: It was designed by Victor Horta for Armand Solvay, the son of the chemist and industrialist Ernest Solvay, and built between 1895 and 1900, in Art Nouveau style.

facts.fact: Horta designed every detail, from furniture, carpets and light fittings to tableware and the doorbell.
facts.quote: He designed every single detail: furniture, carpets, light fittings, tableware and even the doorbell.

facts.fact: He used costly materials such as marble, onyx, bronze and tropical woods.
facts.quote: He used expensive materials such as marble, onyx, bronze, tropical woods, etc.

facts.fact: The pointillist painter Théo van Rysselberghe worked with Horta on the staircase decoration.
facts.quote: For the decoration of the staircase, he cooperated with the pointillist painter Théo van Rysselberghe.

facts.fact: With three other Horta town houses it became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2000.
facts.quote: Together with three other town houses of Victor Horta, including Horta's own house and workshop, it was added to the UNESCO World Heritage list in 2000 as the core of epoch-making urban residences that Horta designed before 1900.

facts.fact: UNESCO notes that these houses are marked by an open plan, the spread of light, and curved decoration joined to the structure.
facts.quote: The stylistic revolution represented by these works is characterised by their open plan, the diffusion of light, and the brilliant joining of the curved lines of decoration with the structure of the building.

facts.fact: The house and most of its contents survived intact thanks to the Wittamer family, who bought it in the 1950s and worked to preserve and restore it.
facts.quote: The Hôtel Solvay and most of its content remained intact thanks to the Wittamer family. They acquired the house in the 1950s and did the utmost to preserve and restore it.

facts.fact: Its facade was restored between March 2022 and October 2024 under architect Barbara Van der Wee.
facts.quote: Major renovation to the façade took place between March 2022 and October 2024 and was carried out under the direction of the architect Barbara Van der Wee and the supervision of Urban.brussels.

facts.fact: The university stands in Bab-Ezzouar, 15 km from Algiers.
facts.quote: The University of Science and Technology – Houari Boumediene (French: Université des sciences et de la technologie Houari-Boumediene, USTHB, Arabic: جامعة العلوم والتكنولوجيا هواري بومدين) is a university located in the town of Bab-Ezzouar 15 kilometres (9.3 mi) from Algiers, Algeria.

facts.fact: The Brazilian architect Oscar Niemeyer designed it, and it was inaugurated in 1974.
facts.quote: The university was designed by Brazilian architect Oscar Niemeyer and was inaugurated in 1974.

facts.fact: It was Algeria's largest university until 2013 and has more than 20,000 students.
facts.quote: USTHB was the largest university in Algeria until 2013; it has over 20,000 students.

facts.fact: Niemeyer opened an office on the Champs-Élysées and found clients in many countries, especially Algeria, where he designed the university.
facts.quote: He opened an office on the Champs-Élysées and found customers in diverse countries, especially in Algeria where he designed the University of Science and Technology-Houari Boumediene.

facts.fact: The university library sits at the centre of the campus.
facts.quote: The University Library is located in the center of the campus.

facts.fact: The library building opened in 1986; when the university opened in 1974, temporary library rooms were set up in the classroom blocks.
facts.quote: In 1974, when the university first opened, temporary library rooms were arranged in the classroom blocks. In 1986, the new library building was officially inaugurated.

facts.fact: Frank Lloyd Wright designed the Ennis House in the Mayan Revival style for Charles and Mabel Ennis; it was completed in 1925 on a hilltop in Los Feliz, Los Angeles.
facts.quote: Designed by the architect Frank Lloyd Wright in the Mayan Revival style for the businessman Charles Ennis and his wife Mabel, it was completed in 1925 on top of a hill in Los Feliz.

facts.fact: It is the largest of the four concrete textile-block houses Wright designed around Los Angeles in the 1920s.
facts.quote: The house is the largest of four concrete textile block houses that Wright designed in Greater Los Angeles in the 1920s, the others being La Miniatura, the Storer House, and the Freeman House.

facts.fact: It was built as Wright was moving from his early Prairie houses toward his later Usonian designs.
facts.quote: The Ennis House was built at a time when Wright was transitioning away from the Prairie-style designs of his early career and toward the Usonian designs of his later career.

facts.fact: The blocks were made of degraded granite from the site, mixed with sand, gravel and water and poured into moulds.
facts.quote: The blocks were made of degraded granite from the site itself, which was mixed with sand, gravel, and water and then poured into molds.

facts.fact: The outer walls step back as they rise, giving the facade the massing of a Mayan temple.
facts.quote: The outer walls contain setbacks as they ascend, giving the facade a massing similar to a Mayan temple.

facts.fact: Its stained-glass windows were the last Wright designed for a house; in later houses he used perforated wood blocks instead.
facts.quote: These were the last stained-glass windows that Wright designed for a residential building during his lifetime, as he began using perforated wood blocks in his later houses.

facts.fact: The plan is laid out on a grid of 4-foot squares, each equal to three textile blocks.
facts.quote: The floor plan is arranged around a grid of squares measuring 4 feet (48 in; 120 cm) across; each square corresponds to three textile blocks.

facts.fact: It is a Los Angeles Historic-Cultural Monument and California Historical Landmark, listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
facts.quote: The Ennis House is a Los Angeles Historic-Cultural Monument and California Historical Landmark, and it is listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

facts.fact: The Süleymaniye Hamam is a historic bathhouse in Istanbul and part of the Süleymaniye Mosque complex.
facts.quote: The Süleymaniye Hamam is a historic hamam (bathhouse) in Istanbul, Turkey, that forms part of the Süleymaniye Mosque complex.

facts.fact: Mimar Sinan built it in 1557 on a hill facing the Golden Horn, for Süleyman the Magnificent, who commissioned it.
facts.quote: The building, on a hill facing the Golden Horn, was built in 1557 by Turkish architect, Mimar Sinan, and was named for his patron, Süleyman the Magnificent, who had commissioned it.

facts.fact: It was nicknamed the 'metalworkers' bath' because workers from nearby foundries bathed there.
facts.quote: It was sometimes called the 'metalworkers' bath' because many workers from the nearby foundries used to frequent it.

facts.fact: The building is arched and domed, with elaborate marble inlay on the walls.
facts.quote: The building is arched and domed, with elaborate marble inlay on the walls.

facts.fact: It has three sections, cold, lukewarm and hot, and the hot section reaches 40–60 °C.
facts.quote: The Sülemaniye Hamam is a traditional bathhouse consisting of three sections: cold, lukewarm and hot. Temperatures in the hot section can reach 40–60 °C (104–140 °F) degrees.

facts.fact: A private cubicle said to have been used by Sinan, who lived near the complex from 1557 to 1588, still survives.
facts.quote: A private cubicle said to have been used by Sinan when he lived near the mosque complex from 1557 to 1588 is still preserved.

facts.fact: The hamam was restored in 2001 to serve tourists.
facts.quote: In 2001, the hamam was restored to cater for tourists.

facts.fact: Alvar Aalto designed the Otaniemi water tower in 1971.
facts.quote: The Otaniemi water tower is a structure designed by the well-known Finnish architect Alvar Aalto in 1971.

facts.fact: It stands in the Otaniemi area of Espoo, Finland.
facts.quote: The water tower is located in Otaniemi area, Espoo, Finland.

facts.fact: The tower holds 6,000 m³ of water and is 45 metres tall.
facts.quote: The total capacity of the tower is 6000 m³.  It rises to a height of 45 meters.

facts.fact: It is Otaniemi's main landmark: a water tank stacked on a free-form, five-storey building holding technical spaces and offices.
facts.quote: It is Otaniemi's principal landmark, and consists of two stacked elements - the water storage tank and a free-form, five-story building constructed underneath containing the technical spaces and offices.

facts.fact: The Osaka Maritime Museum opened on 14 July 2000; work on site began in March 1998.
facts.quote: It was opened by the Mayor of Osaka City on 14 July 2000 having started on site in March 1998.

facts.fact: Paul Andreu proposed setting the museum in the water itself: a basin was dug from reclaimed land so the spherical dome seems to float in the bay, reached by a submerged tunnel.
facts.quote: Upon approaching Paul Andreu he provided preliminary sketches showing a dome, and suggested that the museum should be placed in the water itself and so a 300,000 m² basin was to be excavated from the reclaimed land with a spherical dome seeming to float in the bay, accessed by a submerged tunnel.

facts.fact: Andreu based the dome's geometry on Viviani's curve, with Arup engineering the dome and Tohata the entrance building, tunnel and substructure.
facts.quote: Andreu based the dome on a viviani's curve. Arup were responsible for the design of the structural, mechanical, electrical and seismic engineering solutions for the dome and internal structure holding the exhibits within, whilst Japanese firm Tohata were responsible for the engineering of the entrance building, the submerged tunnel and the dome substructure.

facts.fact: The 20,000 m² building has a landside entry building, a 60 m submerged tunnel and a dome holding four levels.
facts.quote: The final design was for a 20,000 m2 building, consisting of a 5,000 m2 landside entry building, the 60m submerged tunnel of 1,000 m2, opening into the dome, which encased four levels totalling 14,000 m2.

facts.fact: In November 1998 a 4,100-ton floating crane lifted the 1,200-ton dome and its lifting rig onto a barge.
facts.quote: On 3 November 1998 a 4,100 ton floating crane lifted the 1,200 ton dome and lifting rig onto a barge.

facts.fact: Its centrepiece was a replica of the Naniwa Maru, a 17th-century trading ship.
facts.quote: The central exhibit was the replica Naniwa Maru, a 17th-century trade ship or higaki kaisen.

facts.fact: The dome's resistance to earthquake, wave and wind loads won a Structural Special Award from the Institution of Structural Engineers in 2002.
facts.quote: The requirement of the dome to resist seismic, wave, and wind loads and its successful completion, led to the building winning a Structural Special Award in 2002 from the Institution of Structural Engineers, UK.

facts.fact: The museum closed on 10 March 2013 because of financial problems and falling visitor numbers.
facts.quote: The museum was closed on 10 March 2013 because of financial problems, and because the number of visitors had greatly reduced after the museum's initial popularity.

facts.fact: Designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens, the Cenotaph on Whitehall was unveiled in 1920 as the UK's national memorial to the dead of Britain and its Empire in the First World War.
facts.quote: Designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens, it was unveiled in 1920 as the United Kingdom's national memorial to the dead of Britain and the British Empire of the First World War.

facts.fact: 'Cenotaph' means 'empty tomb' in Greek; since most of the dead were buried where they fell, the monument stands for their absence and is a focus for public mourning.
facts.quote: The word cenotaph is derived from Greek, meaning 'empty tomb'. Most of the dead were buried close to where they fell; thus, the Cenotaph symbolises their absence and is a focal point for public mourning.

facts.fact: It began as a temporary structure put up in 1919 for a parade celebrating the end of the war.
facts.quote: The original temporary Cenotaph was erected in 1919 for a parade celebrating the end of the First World War, at which more than 15,000 servicemen, including French and American soldiers, saluted the monument.

facts.fact: For the permanent version Lutyens added entasis (subtle curvature) but otherwise changed the design very little.
facts.quote: Lutyens added entasis (curvature) but otherwise made minimal design alterations.

facts.fact: It is built of Portland stone as a tomb chest on top of a rectangular pylon that narrows as it rises.
facts.quote: The Cenotaph is built from Portland stone. It takes the form of a tomb chest atop a rectangular pylon, which diminishes as it rises.

facts.fact: The memorial is austere, with almost no decoration.
facts.quote: The memorial is austere, containing almost no decoration.

facts.fact: It is a Grade I listed building, part of a national collection of Lutyens's war memorials.
facts.quote: The Cenotaph is a Grade I listed building and forms part of a national collection of Lutyens's war memorials.

facts.fact: It became one of the most influential models for First World War memorials.
facts.quote: While there was no set or agreed standard for First World War memorials, the Cenotaph proved to be one of the most influential models for such structures.

facts.fact: The Tel Aviv Performing Arts Center (Golda Center) on King Saul Boulevard was designed by the Israeli architect Yaakov Rechter.
facts.quote: The Tel Aviv Performing Arts Center (TAPAC, Hebrew: המשכן לאומנויות הבמה) or The Golda Center for Performing Arts (Hebrew: מרכז גולדה לאומנויות הבמה) is a performing arts center at King Saul Boulevard in Tel Aviv, Israel. It was designed by Israeli architect Yaakov Rechter.

facts.fact: It opened in 1994 and is home to the Israeli Opera and the Cameri Theater, a 2003 addition by Rechter Architects.
facts.quote: Opened to the public in 1994, the center is home to the Israeli Opera, and Cameri Theater, a 2003 addition by Rechter Architects, and welcoming about a million visitors annually.

facts.fact: It sits next to Beit Ariela, the central municipal library, and the Tel Aviv Museum of Art, with Dubnow Park behind it.
facts.quote: The complex is adjacent to Beit Ariela (the Central Municipal Library) and the Tel Aviv Museum of Art, with Dubnow Park lying at the back of the center.

facts.fact: It stages dance, classical music, opera and jazz, as well as art exhibitions.
facts.quote: The center hosts a variety of performances including dance, classical music, opera and jazz, as well as fine arts exhibitions.

facts.fact: The center was renovated in the 2010s, with Charles Bronfman as its largest single donor.
facts.quote: Charles Bronfman was the largest single donor who contributed to the renovation of the Tel Aviv Performing Arts Center during the 2010s.

facts.fact: Palazzo dello Strozzino is a Renaissance palace in Florence whose stone facade faces Piazza degli Strozzi, diagonally across from the much larger Palazzo Strozzi.
facts.quote: Palazzo dello Strozzino is a Renaissance palace in Florence, Italy. The stone Renaissance facade is located on Piazza degli Strozzi, diagonal to the Southeast corner of the imposing Palazzo Strozzi.

facts.fact: Once called the Palazzo delle Tre Porte for its three ground-floor doorways, it was a home of the junior branch of the Strozzi family.
facts.quote: The palace, once known as the Palazzo delle Tre Porte for its three ground doorways, was a residence of the cadet branch of the Strozzi family; it was older and smaller than the grandiose Palazzo Strozzi.

facts.fact: A renovation was ordered around 1457 with the design attributed to Brunelleschi; Michelozzo is credited with the lower facade and its irregular rustication.
facts.quote: They ordered a renovation around 1457, with the design attributed to Filippo Brunelleschi, although other architects participated in the construction, including Michelozzo, to whom the lower façade, featuring an irregular rustication, is attributed.

facts.fact: The first floor, with double mullioned windows and gentler rustication, is attributed to Giuliano da Maiano (c. 1456).
facts.quote: The first floor, which has double mullioned windows and a gentler rustication, is attributed to Giuliano da Maiano (c. 1456).

facts.fact: The top floor, in more polished stone, was only added in the 19th century, in the style of similar Renaissance palaces.
facts.quote: The third floor, with more polished stone, was not added until the 19th century, in a style paralleling similar Renaissance palaces.

facts.fact: Michelozzo's colonnaded courtyard of about 1460 was destroyed to make room for a cinema.
facts.quote: Michelozzo also designed the internal courtyard (c. 1460), which had a portico with columns. The courtyard was destroyed to accommodate the cinema.

facts.fact: The palace now holds the Cinema Odeon, designed in 1920 by Marcello Piacentini, and the British Institute of Florence's language school.
facts.quote: The palace houses the Cinema Odeon, designed (1920) by Marcello Piacentini, as well as the language school of the British Institute of Florence.

facts.fact: The Kudrinskaya Square Building is one of Moscow's Seven Sisters, the Stalinist skyscrapers, designed by Mikhail Posokhin and Ashot Mndoyants.
facts.quote: The Kudrinskaya Square Building is a building in Moscow, one of Seven Sisters Of Moscow Stalinist skyscrapers, designed by Mikhail Posokhin (Russian: Михаил Посохин) and  Ashot Mndoyants (Ашот Мндоянц).

facts.fact: Begun in 1950 and completed in 1954, it was the last of the Seven Sisters to be finished.
facts.quote: The skyscraper was laid down in 1950 and completed in 1954. It was the last of the Seven Sisters to be completed.

facts.fact: It is 160 metres tall, with 22 floors in the centre and 18 in the wings.
facts.quote: 160 meters tall, 22 floors (18 usable in the wings and 22 in the central part).

facts.fact: It was built mainly as high-end flats for Soviet cultural leaders, at the end of Krasnaya Presnya street facing the Garden Ring.
facts.quote: The building is located on the end of Krasnaya Presnya street, facing the Sadovoye Koltso and was primarily built as high-end apartments for Soviet cultural leaders rather than politicians.

facts.fact: The building was richly decorated but without a single unified style; its parapets are in the ancient Roman style.
facts.quote: The building was richly decorated but lacked a unified stylistic direction. The parapets are in the ancient Roman style.

facts.fact: The pointed turrets around the spire resemble the domes of an Orthodox church, and sculptures of Soviet workers and soldiers stand on the roof of the podium.
facts.quote: The pointed turrets around the spire resemble the domes of an Eastern Orthodox church. On the roof of the stylobate, there are sculptural portraits of Soviet workers and soldiers.

facts.fact: Besides ventilation, the building had central air conditioning and a central vacuum system piped to every flat.
facts.quote: In addition to the ventilation system, the building had centralised air conditioning. The building was equipped with a centralized dust extraction system, which consisted of brushes and hoses located in each flat, piping running along with the building, and vacuuming stations installed in the basement.

facts.fact: AL_A, Amanda Levete's practice, designed the MAAT in Lisbon for the EDP Foundation.
facts.quote: AL_A has been involved in various notable projects, including the Spencer Dock Bridge in Dublin (completed 2009), MPavilion in Melbourne (2015), the MAAT project in Lisbon for the EDP Foundation (completed 2017), the Central Embassy project in Bangkok (completed 2017), 10 Hill's Place in London (completed 2009) and the pop-up restaurant Tincan (completed 2014), The Dr. Lee Shau Kee Building and William Doo Undergraduate Centre for Wadham College at the University of Oxford (completed 2021), the design for Maggie's cancer care charity building in Southampton (completed 2021) and the media campus for News Corporation in East London.

facts.fact: Forum Groningen is a cultural centre in Groningen holding a library, cinema, museums, study places, a rooftop bar and a restaurant.
facts.quote: Forum Groningen is a cultural center in the city of Groningen in the northern Netherlands that houses a library, cinema, musea, study places, rooftop bar a restaurant and many more.

facts.fact: It opened in November 2019 and receives 2.5 million visitors a year.
facts.quote: Forum Groningen opened in November 2019, and is receiving 2.5 million visitors a year.

facts.fact: It stands next to the Grote Markt and the Nieuwe Markt as part of a wider rebuilding of the city centre.
facts.quote: The center is located next to the Grote Markt Square and the Nieuwe Markt and was part of a larger reconstruction plan in the city center.

facts.fact: The east side of the Grote Markt had been destroyed in the Second World War.
facts.quote: The eastern side of Groningen's Great Market Square was destroyed in World War II.

facts.fact: The design came from a competition: residents picked a top three from seven entries, and the city council chose the winner.
facts.quote: Architects were invited to enter an architectural design competition, allowing the city's inhabitants to put together a top three out of a total of seven designs, from which the Forum's winning design was chosen by a municipal council.

facts.fact: Construction was projected to cost about €71 million, €35 million of it paid by the province.
facts.quote: Construction costs were projected to be around €71 million, of which €35 million was paid by the provincial government.

facts.fact: Earthquakes caused by gas drilling in the Groningen field forced a redesign for earthquake resistance, delaying the building by two years and pushing it over budget.
facts.quote: However, decades' worth of large-scale drilling in the Groningen gas field has led to an increase in induced earthquakes in the province, whose event count shows an exponential growth in time, and caused a budget overrun and construction to run overdue for two years, as new plans had to be drafted to ensure the building's earthquake-resistance.

facts.fact: The building in Regina houses the Legislative Assembly of Saskatchewan.
facts.quote: The Saskatchewan Legislative Building is located in Regina, Saskatchewan, Canada, and houses the Legislative Assembly of Saskatchewan.

facts.fact: It was built between 1908 and 1912 in the Beaux-Arts style to a design by Edward and William Sutherland Maxwell of Montreal.
facts.quote: The Saskatchewan Legislative Building was built between 1908 and 1912 in the Beaux-Arts style to a design by Edward and William Sutherland Maxwell of Montreal.

facts.fact: The design allows the building to grow with wings running south from each end to enclose a courtyard.
facts.quote: The design contemplates expansion of the building by the addition of wings extending south from the east and west ends and coming together to form a courtyard.

facts.fact: It was meant to be red brick, but Premier Walter Scott switched to Manitoba Tyndall stone for greater grandeur, adding $50,000 to the cost.
facts.quote: The plans originally called for the exterior of the building to be red brick but after construction had begun and red bricks were already on the site, Premier Walter Scott decided that Manitoba Tyndall stone would give the building greater grandeur and the plans were adjusted with the substitution increasing the building cost by $50,000.

facts.fact: The chamber was designed for 125 members, but the assembly has never had more than 66.
facts.quote: Such planning is evident in the legislative chamber itself, designed to accommodate 125 members. The assembly has never expanded beyond 66 MLAs (and currently has 61).

facts.fact: From 1965 Clifford Wiens led a renovation and restoration that took about fourteen years.
facts.quote: In 1965, Clifford Wiens started a major project of renovation and restoration which took some fourteen years to complete.

facts.fact: It overlooks Wascana Lake.
facts.quote: The Saskatchewan Legislative Building is located at 2405 Legislative Drive, Regina, overlooking Wascana Lake.

facts.fact: The building and its grounds became a National Historic Site of Canada in 2005.
facts.quote: The legislative building and its grounds were designated a National Historic Site of Canada in 2005.

facts.fact: Nuevos Ministerios is a government complex in central Madrid.
facts.quote: Nuevos Ministerios (English: New Ministries) is a government complex in central Madrid, Spain.

facts.fact: Secundino Zuazo designed it, with backing from the Minister of Public Works Indalecio Prieto; begun in 1933 and halted by the Civil War, it was completed in 1942.
facts.quote: The original project was the work of the architect Secundino Zuazo Ugalde and was soon sponsored by the then Minister of Public Works, Indalecio Prieto. Its construction began in 1933 and, although it was paralyzed during the Civil War, the entire complex was completed in 1942.

facts.fact: As part of Madrid's expansion plan, the old racecourse, which stood in the way of the Paseo de la Castellana, was demolished.
facts.quote: As part of this purpose, the old racecourse, which was an obstacle to the planning of Paseo de la Castellana, was demolished.

facts.fact: Zuazo took the Escorial monastery as his inspiration.
facts.quote: Zuazo took the Escorial as an inspiration for the project.

facts.fact: It was finished by a team of architects linked to the new regime, who removed or changed important parts such as a skyscraper planned for the north side.
facts.quote: This was finalized by a team of architects related to the new regime, which eliminated or modified important parts of the project, such as the skyscraper planned for the north side.

facts.fact: The complex is arranged around a large central open space with fountains and ponds, with a long arcade facing the Paseo de la Castellana.
facts.quote: The complex consists of a large central space with open spaces, fountains and ponds, around which different ministries are arranged, as well as a large arcade on the side facing Paseo de la Castellana.

facts.fact: Nuevos Ministerios station was dug out beneath the central courtyard.
facts.quote: Underneath the patio was excavated the one that at the moment is the station of Nuevos Ministerios.

facts.fact: Zuazo was a rationalist architect, and Nuevos Ministerios is among his best-known works, though he did not direct its construction.
facts.quote: Zuazo was a rationalist architect, among the most important of his generation. The best known of his works are the Casa de las Flores and Nuevos Ministerios of Madrid (whose construction he did not direct).

facts.fact: The Hansahochhaus is a skyscraper in the Neustadt-Nord quarter of Cologne.
facts.quote: The Hansahochhaus is a skyscraper in the Neustadt-Nord quarter of north-central Cologne.

facts.fact: Built in 1924–25, it was Cologne's first skyscraper and one of the first in Germany.
facts.quote: When constructed in 1924-25 it was the city's first skyscraper, and one of the first skyscrapers in Germany.

facts.fact: The local architect Jacob Koerfer designed it as an Expressionist office building.
facts.quote: It was designed as an office building in the Expressionist style by the local architect, Jacob Koerfer.

facts.fact: With 17 floors and a height of 65 metres, it was briefly Europe's tallest building.
facts.quote: With 17 floors and a total height of 65 meters, for a brief period following its construction the Hansahochhaus was Europe's tallest building.

facts.fact: It is a protected historic monument.
facts.quote: It is currently protected under historic monument legislation.

facts.fact: Oakland City Hall, completed in 1914, is 98 m tall and was the first high-rise government building in the United States.
facts.quote: The current building was completed in 1914, and replaced a prior building that stood on what is now Frank H. Ogawa Plaza. Standing at the height of 320 feet (98 m), it was the first high-rise government building in the United States.

facts.fact: When built, it was the tallest building west of the Mississippi.
facts.quote: At the time it was built, it was also the tallest building west of the Mississippi River.

facts.fact: The New York firm Palmer & Hornbostel designed it in 1910 after winning a national competition.
facts.quote: The building was designed by New York–based architecture firm Palmer & Hornbostel in 1910, after winning a nationwide design competition.

facts.fact: The Beaux-Arts building is said to resemble a rectangular wedding cake and has three tiers.
facts.quote: The building, constructed in the Beaux-Arts style, resembles a "rectangular wedding cake". It consists of three tiers.

facts.fact: The thinner second tier is a ten-storey office tower whose top floor held a 36-cell jail, unused since the 1960s; above it sits a two-storey podium with a clock tower.
facts.quote: The thinner second tier follows; it is a ten-story office tower. The top floor of this section (the 12th floor) houses a 36-cell jail with an outdoor yard that has gone unused since the 1960s. Above the second tier is the two-story podium with a clock tower on top.

facts.fact: The outside is white granite and terracotta; inside is white and black marble.
facts.quote: The exterior is built of white granite and terra cotta, while the inside is built of white and black marble.

facts.fact: It was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1983.
facts.quote: In 1983, the Oakland City Hall was added to the National Register of Historic Places.

facts.fact: In the seismic retrofit, steel columns in the foundation were cut and replaced with rubber bearings, and the building can now move 18–20 inches sideways in an earthquake.
facts.quote: To do so, steel columns in the foundation were cut and they were replaced by rubber bearings. Steel beams were added to support the steel structure and concrete walls were added to support existing walls. The building can now move laterally 18-20 inches in an earthquake.

facts.fact: Rosenbad is a state-owned building in central Stockholm that serves as the seat of the Swedish Government.
facts.quote: It is a building owned by the Swedish state and serves as the seat of the Government.

facts.fact: It stands on Strömgatan on the north bank of the Norrström; the Art Nouveau architect Ferdinand Boberg designed it, and it was completed in 1902.
facts.quote: Rosenbad is located on Strömgatan on the north side of the river Norrström. It was designed by Art Nouveau architect Ferdinand Boberg, and completed in 1902.

facts.fact: It first held a mix of uses, including a restaurant of the same name until 1956.
facts.quote: It originally housed a variety of functions, including a restaurant (until 1956) of the same name.

facts.fact: It now houses the Prime Minister's Office and the Government Offices.
facts.quote: Rosenbad now functions as the seat for the Prime Minister's Office and the Government Offices.

facts.fact: The Parliament House and the Royal Palace lie across the water of Stockholms ström.
facts.quote: The Parliament House and the Royal Palace are located across the waters of Stockholms ström.

facts.fact: Joshua Ramus designed the Perelman Performing Arts Center at the World Trade Center in New York.
facts.quote: Ramus has designed renowned buildings including the Perelman Performing Arts Center at the World Trade Center in New York, New York; The Lindemann Performing Arts Center at Brown University in Providence, Rhode Island; the AT&T Performing Arts Center Dee & Charles Wyly Theatre in Dallas, Texas; the Vakko Fashion Center & Power Media Headquarters in Istanbul, Turkey; the Seattle Central Library in Washington state; and the Guggenheim-Hermitage Museum in Las Vegas, Nevada.

facts.fact: REX's building is 80,000 sq ft, made for producing and premiering theatre, dance, music, musical theatre, opera and film.
facts.quote: Ongoing projects include the Performing Arts Center at the World Trade Center, an 80,000 sq ft (7,400 m2) building for the production and premiering of theater, dance, music, musical theater, opera, and film works; the Mercedes-Benz Future Lab in Stuttgart, Germany, a 110,000 sq ft (10,200 m2) public showcase for the brand's impact on mobility and a factory for debating the future; a 46,000 sq ft (4,300 m2) private residence on Long Island; 2050 M Street, a new office building in Washington, DC, and a performing arts center at Brown University.

facts.fact: Tournay Abbey is an active Benedictine monastery in Tournay, Hautes-Pyrénées.
facts.quote: Tournay Abbey (French: Abbaye Notre-Dame de Tournay) is an active Benedictine monastery in Tournay, Hautes-Pyrénées, France.

facts.fact: The community, founded in Madiran in the 1930s, moved to Tournay in 1952, and the building was completed in 1958.
facts.quote: A new abbey was founded in the 1930s in Madiran and was transferred to Tournay in 1952, the year after construction of a new monastery. The building was completed in 1958.

facts.fact: About 20 monks live there.
facts.quote: The abbey remains active and houses a community of approximately 20 monks.

facts.fact: Heureka is a science centre in Tikkurila, Vantaa, designed by Heikkinen – Komonen Architects, at the meeting of the main railway line and the river Keravanjoki.
facts.quote: Heureka is a science center in the Tikkurila district of Vantaa, Finland, north of Helsinki, designed by Heikkinen – Komonen Architects. It is located at the intersection of the Finnish Main Line and the river Keravanjoki.

facts.fact: The design won a 1985 competition; it was submitted by Mikko Heikkinen, Markku Komonen and Lauri Anttila.
facts.quote: An architectural competition, held in 1985, turned out two first prizes from which the winning design was selected; namely the "Heureka" design submitted by Mikko Heikkinen, Markku Komonen and Lauri Anttila.

facts.fact: The building covers 8,200 m², 2,800 m² of it exhibition space, and opened on 28 April 1989.
facts.quote: The overall area of the building is 8,200 m², of which 2,800 m² is exhibition space. The Finnish Science Centre Heureka opened its doors to the public on 28 April 1989.

facts.fact: The facade facing the railway uses mirror glass to shield the building from train noise.
facts.quote: The facade of the building facing the railway track makes use of mirror glass, intended to shield the building from the noise caused by the trains.

facts.fact: Its focus is a 14-metre-tall cylindrical exhibition hall.
facts.quote: The central inner space and architectural focus point of the science centre is its 14-metre-tall cylindrical exhibition hall.

facts.fact: Each column is a cluster of slimmer columns, four in the middle, two at edges and one at corners, to show how the load is shared.
facts.quote: Its pillars consist of sub-pillars, with four in the central area, two on each edge and one in each corner. This structure is intended to visualise the relative distribution of load.

facts.fact: Each part of the building has its own structural system, mixing concrete, steel and wood.
facts.quote: Each part of the building is fitted with a structural system developed specifically for it. In terms of structures and materials, the science centre is a kind of a conglomeration. It contains concrete, steel and wood constructs.

facts.fact: The cylindrical main hall was inspired by an exhibition Gunnar Asplund designed at the Stockholm city library.
facts.quote: The cylindrical main exhibition hall was inspired by an exhibition designed by Gunnar Asplund at the Stockholm city library and houses about 200 exhibits related to different fields of science.

facts.fact: The Historical Museum of the Palatinate is in Speyer, across the square from Speyer Cathedral.
facts.quote: It is situated across the square from the Speyer Cathedral.

facts.fact: It covers the history of the Palatinate with about a million objects, the oldest a hand axe around 190,000 years old.
facts.quote: The museum's focus is on the History of the Palatinate; it has a collection of about 1 million artifacts, the oldest being an approximately 190,000-year-old hand axe.

facts.fact: The museum was founded in 1869 by combining the collections of the Historical Society of the Palatinate, the former Rhine District and the City of Speyer.
facts.quote: The museum was established in 1869 and the collections of the Historical Society of the Palatinate, the former Rhine District, and the City of Speyer were combined.

facts.fact: Gabriel von Seidl built the present building in 1910, and a modern annex was added in 1990.
facts.quote: The building at the present site was built in 1910 by architect Gabriel von Seidl; a modern annex was added in 1990.

facts.fact: Speyer made Seidl an honorary citizen in 1909 for the new museum building.
facts.quote: Seidl was made an honorary citizen of Speyer on 14 April 1909 because of his construction of a new building for the Historical Museum of the Palatinate in Speyer.

facts.fact: Its five permanent exhibitions fill 8,000 m².
facts.quote: The five permanent exhibitions covering 8,000 m2 are: Prehistory, Roman Era, Cathedral Treasure, Modern Era and the Wine Museum.

facts.fact: A 650 m² covered courtyard, the Forum, hosts concerts, workshops, theatre and talks.
facts.quote: The 650 m2-area of covered courtyard offers opportunities for communication, concerts, workshops, theatre, discussions etc.

facts.fact: The inn has a multi-storey log lobby flanked by long framed wings of guest rooms.
facts.quote: The Inn has a multi-story log lobby, flanked by long frame wings containing guest rooms.

facts.fact: With its log-and-limb lobby and huge stone fireplace, it exemplifies the rustic resort style also called National Park Service Rustic.
facts.quote: With its log and limb lobby and massive (500-short-ton or 450-metric-ton, 85-foot or 26-meter) stone fireplace, the inn is an example of the "Golden Age" of rustic resort architecture, a style which is also known as National Park Service Rustic.

facts.fact: It was built over the winter of 1903–04 largely from local lodgepole pine and rhyolite stone.
facts.quote: Initial construction was carried out over the winter of 1903–1904, largely using locally obtained materials including lodgepole pine and rhyolite stone.

facts.fact: It is the largest log hotel in the world, and possibly the largest log building.
facts.quote: The structure is the largest log hotel in the world; possibly even the largest log building in the world.

facts.fact: Its architect was the 29-year-old Robert Reamer of the Yellowstone Park Company.
facts.quote: The inn's architect was 29-year-old Robert Reamer, an architect for the Yellowstone Park Company, which was affiliated with the Northern Pacific Railway.

facts.fact: The Old House is turned 90 degrees to the geyser so that the entrance porch frames a view of Old Faithful for arriving visitors.
facts.quote: The Old House is rotated 90 degrees with respect to Old Faithful so that a view of the geyser is framed by the entrance porch for arriving visitors.

facts.fact: Twisted and curved branches brace the framing inside and out, giving the building a strongly rustic feel.
facts.quote: Both interior and exterior framing is supported by twisted or curved branches, giving the entire structure a strongly rustic air.

facts.fact: Harry Child hired Reamer to design a much more radical building, with roots in the rustic camps of the Adirondacks.
facts.quote: Child instead hired Reamer to design a much more radical building with antecedents in the rustic camps of the Adirondacks.

facts.fact: The Museum Yamato Bunkakan is a museum of Asian art in Nara.
facts.quote: The Museum of Japanese Art Yamato Bunkakan (大和文華館, Yamato bunkakan) is a museum of Asian art in Nara, Nara.

facts.fact: It was founded in 1960 to keep and show the private collection of the Kintetsu railway company.
facts.quote: The museum was established in 1960 to preserve and display the private collection of Kintetsu Corporation (named Kinki Nippon Railway Co., Ltd. till June 27, 2003).

facts.fact: Its holdings number more than twenty thousand objects, from sculpture and ceramics to paintings and calligraphy.
facts.quote: This museum of Asian art has holdings of more than twenty thousand objects of sculpture, ceramics, lacquer, paintings, prints, textiles and calligraphy.

facts.fact: The Vatroslav Lisinski Concert Hall is a large concert hall and convention centre in Zagreb, named after the 19th-century Croatian composer.
facts.quote: Vatroslav Lisinski Concert Hall (Croatian: Koncertna dvorana Vatroslava Lisinskog) is a large concert hall and convention center in Zagreb, Croatia. It is named after Vatroslav Lisinski, a 19th-century Croatian composer.

facts.fact: It has a large hall of 1,841 seats, a small hall of 305 seats, and a big lobby that doubles as an exhibition space.
facts.quote: The building has a big hall with 1,841 seats and a small hall with 305 seats. A large lobby doubles as an exhibition area.

facts.fact: The decision to build was made in 1957, and a team led by Marijan Haberle won the design competition.
facts.quote: The decision to build a new multifunctional hall in Zagreb was made in 1957. A team of architects led by Marijan Haberle won the design contest.

facts.fact: Building began in 1961, but flooding and money troubles delayed it until it opened on 29 December 1973.
facts.quote: The construction began in 1961, but flooding and financial difficulties pushed the completion date into the next decade. The hall was finally opened on 29 December 1973.

facts.fact: It is Haberle's best-known work.
facts.quote: His best known work is the Concert Hall Vatroslav Lisinski in Zagreb.

facts.fact: It hosted the 1990 Eurovision Song Contest after its first major renovation in 1989; its copper roof was fully replaced in 1992.
facts.quote: Vatroslav Lisinski Concert Hall was the venue of the 1990 Eurovision Song Contest, after its first major renovation in 1989. In 1992, the hall's copper roof cover was completely replaced.

facts.fact: The hall received 10 million visitors in its first thirty years.
facts.quote: The hall saw 10 million visitors in the first thirty years of operation.

facts.fact: The Jewish Museum Munich is part of the city's new Jewish Center on Sankt-Jakobs-Platz.
facts.quote: The Jewish Museum Munich (Hebrew: המוזיאון היהודי במינכן), provides an overview of Munich’s Jewish history and is part of the city's new Jewish Center located at Sankt-Jakobs-Platz in Munich, Germany.

facts.fact: It stands between the Ohel Jakob synagogue and the Jewish Community Center.
facts.quote: It is situated between the main Ohel Jakob synagogue and the Jewish Community Center which is home to the Jewish Community of Munich and Upper Bavaria and houses a public elementary school, a kindergarten, a youth center as well as a community auditorium and a kosher restaurant.

facts.fact: It was built from 2004 and opened on 22 March 2007; the city of Munich runs it.
facts.quote: The museum was built from 2004 until its inauguration on 22 March 2007 and is run by the city of Munich.

facts.fact: The three-building complex was designed by Rena Wandel-Hoefer and Wolfgang Lorch, who won a competition in 2001.
facts.quote: The Jewish Museum Munich is part of a complex consisting of three buildings and was designed by architects Rena Wandel-Hoefer and Wolfgang Lorch who were awarded the contract after an architecture competition on 6 July 2001.

facts.fact: The museum is a freestanding cube with a transparent ground-floor lobby.
facts.quote: The museum is designed as a freestanding cube with a transparent ground floor lobby.

facts.fact: The two upper floors hold changing exhibitions, a learning centre and a library, while the permanent exhibition is on the lower level.
facts.quote: The two top floors house changing exhibitions, a learning center, and a library. The museum’s permanent exhibition is located on the lower level.

facts.fact: It cost about €17.2 million, funded by the city of Munich.
facts.quote: It cost about €17.2 million to build with funding provided by the city of Munich.

facts.fact: The Royal Armouries Museum in Leeds holds the UK's National Collection of Arms and Armour.
facts.quote: The Royal Armouries Museum in Leeds, West Yorkshire, England, is a national museum that holds the National Collection of Arms and Armour.

facts.fact: It is a £42.5 million purpose-built museum at Leeds Dock that opened in 1996; the collection was previously at the Tower of London.
facts.quote: The Royal Armouries Museum is a £42.5 million purpose-built museum located in Leeds Dock that opened in 1996. Its collection was previously on display or in storage at the Tower of London where the Royal Armouries still maintains a presence and displays in the White Tower.

facts.fact: It was designed by Derek Walker and Buro Happold, built by Alfred McAlpine, and opened by Queen Elizabeth II in March 1996.
facts.quote: RAI commissioned a new building to accommodate the museum: it was designed by Derek Walker and Buro Happold, and built by Alfred McAlpine at a cost of £42.5 million and was officially opened by Queen Elizabeth II in March 1996.

facts.fact: It was one of the first projects under the UK's private finance initiative.
facts.quote: The museum was one of the first projects carried out under the UK private finance initiative: a non-departmental public body, the Royal Armouries, contracted with a private sector company, Royal Armouries International (RAI), which would build and then operate the museum for 60 years in return for the ticket revenue.

facts.fact: On the south bank of the River Aire, it is a focal point of the regenerated Leeds waterfront.
facts.quote: Situated close to Leeds city centre on the South bank of the River Aire the museum is one of the focal points of the regenerated Leeds waterfront.

facts.fact: It was designed from the inside out: ceilings, up to 6.5 m high, were set to fit the longest staff weapons displayed upright.
facts.quote: The Royal Armouries Museum itself was designed from the inside out. The ceiling heights of the new building were designed to accommodate the longest staff weapons in the collections, displayed vertically, and are 6.5 meters off the ground at their highest point.

facts.fact: The Hall of Steel is a giant staircase whose walls carry trophy displays of 2,500 objects, recalling those of the Tower Armouries.
facts.quote: In addition to the five original galleries which house 5,000 objects in the permanent displays and the Peace Gallery, the museum also includes the Hall of Steel, a giant staircase whose walls are decorated with trophy displays composed of 2,500 objects reminiscent of the historical trophy displays erected by the Tower Armouries from the 17th century.

facts.fact: A 150 m jousting arena runs alongside the River Aire.
facts.quote: Running alongside the River Aire for 490 feet (150 m), with seating on the land-ward side, is the Jousting Arena: though the museum no longer has its own horses, two important jousting contests each year are still held with competitors from all over the world.

facts.fact: Monona Terrace is a convention centre on the shore of Lake Monona in Madison, Wisconsin, first proposed by Frank Lloyd Wright in 1938 and opened in 1997.
facts.quote: Initially proposed by Wisconsin-born architect Frank Lloyd Wright in 1938, the 250,000 square feet (23,000 m2) building opened in 1997 and attracts nearly 400,000 visitors annually.

facts.fact: Wright's 1938 proposal was rejected by the Dane County board by one vote.
facts.quote: Monona Terrace was originally designed and proposed by Frank Lloyd Wright in 1938 but rejected by the Dane County development board by one vote.

facts.fact: Wright kept campaigning for the plan and reworking its design until his death in 1959.
facts.quote: Wright would continue to seek support for the plan and alter its design until his death in 1959.

facts.fact: Mayor Paul Soglin revived Wright's proposal in 1990.
facts.quote: In 1990, Madison mayor Paul Soglin resurrected Wright's proposal.

facts.fact: Opponents argued it was not a genuine Wright building, too costly, and would block the view of Lake Monona from the Capitol Square.
facts.quote: Among the arguments against its construction, opponents argued that it was not a genuine Wright building, that the costs were too steep for the taxpayers to bear and that the construction would adversely affect the environment, specifically destroying the view of Lake Monona from street level on the south side of the Capitol Square.

facts.fact: The exterior follows Wright's design, while the interior was designed by former Wright apprentice Anthony Puttnam of Taliesin Associated Architects.
facts.quote: Although the exterior design is Wright's, the interior as executed was designed by former Wright apprentice Anthony Puttnam of Taliesin Associated Architects.

facts.fact: It opened on 18 July 1997, nearly 60 years after Wright first proposed it.
facts.quote: Monona Terrace Community and Convention Center opened on July 18, 1997, nearly 60 years after the design was first proposed by Wright.

facts.fact: It is two blocks from the Wisconsin State Capitol, and its roof looks over downtown Madison, the Capitol and Lake Monona.
facts.quote: Monona Terrace is located two blocks from the Wisconsin State Capitol building in downtown Madison. From the roof of Monona Terrace, one can see downtown Madison, including the Capitol and Lake Monona.

facts.fact: The Minnaert university building in Utrecht was nominated for the Rietveld Award in 1999.
facts.quote: Nomination for the Rietveld Award | for Minnaert University Building Utrecht | 1999

facts.fact: The Zénith de Lille is a multi-purpose indoor arena seating up to 7,000, one of the largest venues in Lille.
facts.quote: The Zénith de Lille (originally Zénith Arena) is a multi-purpose indoor arena in Lille, France. Its ability to seat up to 7,000 people makes it one of the largest venues in Lille.

facts.fact: Rem Koolhaas designed it with Cecil Balmond; it opened in 1994 as part of the Lille Grand Palais, alongside a congress centre and exhibition halls.
facts.quote: Designed by the Dutch architect Rem Koolhaas with Cecil Balmond and inaugurated in 1994, the Zénith Arena is a part of the cultural complex Lille Grand Palais which includes two other spaces: a congress center and exhibition halls.

facts.fact: Koolhaas worked with Renz van Luxemburg on acoustics, dUCKS scéno on scenography and Arup on engineering.
facts.quote: Rem Koolhaas surrounded himself with Renz van Luxemburg for the acoustic studies, dUCKS scéno for the scenography and Arup Group for the engineering studies.

facts.fact: The arena was a long-term project of Lille's former mayor Pierre Mauroy.
facts.quote: The arena was a long term project commissioned by former mayor of Lille, Pierre Mauroy.

facts.fact: The project began in 1980 but was not finished until June 1994.
facts.quote: The project began in 1980 however it was not completed until June 1994.

facts.fact: The Koolhaas-designed venue holds three auditoriums, 28 meeting rooms, a banquet hall and the Zénith Arena.
facts.quote: The venue, designed by Rem Koolhaas, contains three auditoriums, 28 meetings rooms, a banquet hall and the Zénith Arena.

facts.fact: He Art Museum in Shunde, Foshan, is a privately funded non-profit museum designed by Tadao Ando.
facts.quote: He Art Museum, located in Shunde, Foshan, Guangdong Province, China, He Art Museum (or HEM, Chinese: 和美术馆) is a privately funded non-profit museum designed by Pritzker Prize winner Tadao Ando.

facts.fact: Its name, He, means harmony and is the family name of its founder, He Jianfeng.
facts.quote: Meaning harmony, balance and mixture, the museum's name "He" (Chinese: 和) takes the family name of its founder, He Jianfeng, son of Midea Group founder He Xiangjian.

facts.fact: It has about 16,000 m² of floor space, around half of it for exhibitions.
facts.quote: The museum has a total floor area of about 16,000 square metres (172,000 sq ft), of which about 8,000 square metres (86,000 sq ft) is exhibition space.

facts.fact: Ando drew the circle motif from Lingnan building traditions.
facts.quote: Ando took the circle motif from Lingnan building traditions and patterns.

facts.fact: The exterior is four concentric rings that widen off-centre as they rise, like ripples on water.
facts.quote: The exterior is formed by four concentric rings that widen eccentrically from the ground upwards, like ripples spreading on water; Ando said the design took the region's subtropical climate into account, giving the building strong effects of light and shadow.

facts.fact: A circular reflecting pool tempers the summer heat and acts as the building's visual base.
facts.quote: A reflecting pool echoing the circular form tempers the subtropical summer heat and, with the building mirrored in it, serves as its visual base.

facts.fact: Its centrepiece is a double-helix staircase of cast-in-place fair-faced concrete in the central atrium, lit from the dome above.
facts.quote: The centrepiece is a double-helix staircase in the central atrium, cast in place in fair-faced concrete and lit by natural light from the dome above.

facts.fact: The New Synagogue in Mainz is a synagogue and Jewish community centre on Synagogenplatz.
facts.quote: The New Synagogue (German: Neuen Synagoge) is a Jewish congregation, community center, and synagogue, located on Synagogenplatz, Mainz in the state of Rhineland-Palatinate, in Germany.

facts.fact: The Modernist building was put up in 2010 on the site of the former main synagogue, destroyed in 1938.
facts.quote: The Modernist-styled building was erected in 2010, on the site of the former main synagogue, destroyed in 1938, on the Hindenburgstraße of Mainz Neustadt.

facts.fact: Manuel Herz won the 1999 competition to design the synagogue and community centre.
facts.quote: In 1999, there was a competition to design a new synagogue building and a Jewish community centre. The winner was architect Manuel Herz.

facts.fact: The building reflects the liturgical word Kedushah (sanctification), and Herz used its five Hebrew letters to shape the five parts of the community centre.
facts.quote: The building reflects the Jewish-liturgical term Kedushah (Hebrew: קדושה, romanized: sanctification and exaltation). Cologne architect, Manuel Herz, intended to symbolize this with the five Hebrew letters the five ranges of the Jewish center for community events, adult education and as Hebrew school for school children.

facts.fact: The horn-shaped roof of the prayer hall points east towards Jerusalem and represents a shofar.
facts.quote: The eastward-directed, (towards Jerusalem), horn-shaped roof of the assembly place represents a shofar.

facts.fact: The prayer hall seats about 450, five times the previous capacity.
facts.quote: The prayer sanctuary of the New Synagogue offers approximately 450 places which corresponds to five times the previous prayer capacity.

facts.fact: It opened on 3 September 2010, the anniversary of the old synagogue's 1912 inauguration.
facts.quote: The inauguration was held on September 3, 2010, following weather delays; this date was the anniversary of the inauguration of the former synagogue in 1912.

facts.fact: It was nominated for the Mies van der Rohe Prize for European Architecture.
facts.quote: The building received the nomination for the Mies van der Rohe Prize for European Architecture, German Facade Prize 2011.

facts.fact: The Paulinum is a University of Leipzig building, begun in 2007, on the site of the university church destroyed in 1968 under East Germany's communist regime.
facts.quote: The Paulinum is a university building of University of Leipzig, whose construction began in 2007. Today's Paulinum stands at the site of the old university church, the Paulinerkirche, which was destroyed in 1968 during the communist regime of East Germany.

facts.fact: Erick van Egeraat designed it.
facts.quote: The building was designed by award-winning architect Erick van Egeraat.

facts.fact: It holds the university's assembly hall with an oratory, plus rooms for the information science and mathematics faculties.
facts.quote: The Paulinum contains the university's assembly hall with an oratory, as well as rooms of the faculties for information science and mathematics.

facts.fact: The assembly hall stands exactly where the old church stood and displays figures and objects saved from it.
facts.quote: The assembly hall, which was erected on exactly the same site as the old university church, exhibits figures and other objects from Paulinerkirche and offers a room of common prayer.

facts.fact: Its facade uses collegiate Gothic forms in memory of the original church.
facts.quote: The facade of the Paulinum features collegiate Gothic architecture as a commemoration of the original building.

facts.fact: Its organ, by Jehmlich Orgelbau Dresden, was completed in 2017.
facts.quote: Construction of the instrument was by Jehmlich Orgelbau Dresden (opus 1161) and was completed in 2017.

facts.fact: The Spiral House is an apartment complex in Ramat Gan, Israel, designed by Zvi Hecker.
facts.quote: The Spiral House (Hebrew: בית הספירלה, Beit HaSpirala) is an apartment complex in Ramat Gan, Israel, designed by the architect Zvi Hecker.

facts.fact: The complex rises as an upward spiral; Hecker designed it with Gil Bernstein, Shmuel Groberman and Rina Hering.
facts.quote: The complex has a form of an upward spiral; it was built by Jaakov Hai and designed by the architect Zvi Hecker in collaboration with Gil Bernstein, Shmuel Groberman, and Rina Hering.

facts.fact: It uses terracing like that of Arab villages, where roofs serve as living space.
facts.quote: The house "deploys the principle of terracing typical of Arab villages where the roof is used as part of the living space for the apartments".

facts.fact: It was built from 1984 to 1990.
facts.quote: Construction took place from 1984 to 1990.

facts.fact: It is built of concrete, faced with plaster, pink glass, stone fragments and corrugated tin.
facts.quote: The building was built in concrete, "with a facade of plaster, pink glass and stone fragments and corrugated tin."

facts.fact: Hecker called it a 'miniature Tower of Babel'.
facts.quote: Hecker described the building as a "miniature Tower of Babel"; Shmuel Grobstein, who participated in the design, said that it "looks like a storm passed through Ramat Gan, picking up all the wrecks from the roofs and yards, and created the spiral in one swoop."

facts.fact: Hecker won the Rechter Prize for architecture in 1999 for the building.
facts.quote: Hecker won the Rechter Prize for architecture in 1999 for the Spiral House.

facts.fact: Hecker lived in the Dubiner House opposite, and changed the design several times while it was being built.
facts.quote: Hecker himself lived in the Dubiner house which is opposite the Spiral House. During the construction, he therefore kept an explicit control and changed the design several times during construction.

facts.fact: The STC Group, a maritime transport and logistics education provider, has its headquarters in Rotterdam.
facts.quote: The group's headquarters is located in Rotterdam, the Netherlands.

facts.fact: Its founding school, the Shipping and Transport College, came from a 1990 merger of all Dutch maritime colleges.
facts.quote: The founding school, Shipping and Transport College, is the result of a merger of all Dutch maritime colleges in 1990.

facts.fact: Neutelings Riedijk Architects designed its new building in the Lloyd District, a historic and contemporary port area in central Rotterdam.
facts.quote: Since the mergers in 1990 the STC Group opened many new buildings including a new building in the Lloyd District by Neutelings Riedijk Architects, a historical and contemporary port area in the center of Rotterdam.

facts.fact: The building holds all the simulators and training equipment for secondary and higher shipping and transport education.
facts.quote: This building has all the simulators and training materials required for secondary and higher shipping and transport education.

facts.fact: It is a Rotterdam architectural landmark, opened by King Willem-Alexander.
facts.quote: The building is a Rotterdam architectural landmark and was opened by King Willem-Alexander of the Netherlands.

facts.fact: The Museu de Arte do Rio (MAR) is an art museum in Rio de Janeiro, inaugurated on 1 March 2013.
facts.quote: Museu de Arte do Rio (MAR) (English: Art Museum of Rio) is an art museum in Rio de Janeiro which was inaugurated on 1 March 2013.

facts.fact: It is part of a project, begun in 2009, to revitalise downtown Rio.
facts.quote: The museum is part of a project to revitalize downtown Rio de Janeiro which began in 2009 through a municipal law that intended to invest up to R$8 billion real in the years following its passage.

facts.fact: Jacobsen Arquitetura planned it, led by Paulo Jacobsen, Bernardo Jacobsen and Thiago Bernardes.
facts.quote: The entire architectural plan was organized by Jacobsen Arquitetura, with ideas made by three main architects: Paulo Jacobsen, Bernardo Jacobsen, and Thiago Bernardes.

facts.fact: It occupies two buildings on Praça Mauá, between the city centre and the port zone.
facts.quote: It is located in the historic downtown and occupies two buildings at Praça Mauá, between Centro and the Zona Portuária.

facts.fact: One of them is the Palacete Dom João VI, built in an eclectic style.
facts.quote: One of the buildings is the Palacete Dom João VI, constructed with an eclectic style.

facts.fact: The other, a former bus station next to the palace, houses the Escola do Olhar art school and the offices.
facts.quote: The other, adjacent to the palace, was used as the Mariano Procópio bus station prior to being integrated into the museum, the "Escola do Olhar", along with housing the administrative offices and other departments.

facts.fact: The two buildings are joined by a suspended walkway and a 'fluid cover' roof.
facts.quote: The two buildings are connected by a suspended catwalk, a "fluid cover", which occupies a total area of 2,300 square meters and a constructed area of 11,240 m².

facts.fact: In 2013 it won the Architizer A+ Award for the best museum project, against the Heydar Aliyev Center, the new Rijksmuseum and others.
facts.quote: The museum was awarded, in the year of its inauguration in 2013, the best construction project of the year in the museum category for the Architizer A+ Awards.  The Museu de Arte do Rio competed with the Heydar Aliyev Center, New Rijksmuseum, the Zhujiajiao Museum of Humanities & Arts, and the Danish Maritime Museum.

facts.fact: Alvar and Elissa Aalto won Seinäjoki's 1959 competition, which included plans for a library, a theatre and a state office building.
facts.quote: Alvar Aalto and his wife, Elissa Aalto, won the follow-up competition in 1959, which also included plans for a library, a theatre, and a state office building.

facts.fact: Alvar Aalto finished the theatre's plans in 1969, but it was built only in 1986–1987, under Elissa Aalto's guidance, after his death in 1976.
facts.quote: The plans for the theatre were finished by Aalto in 1969, but the building was only realized almost two decades later in 1986–1987 and under the guidance of Elissa Aalto, as Alvar Aalto had died in 1976.

facts.fact: The theatre (1987) is the last of the six buildings of the Aalto Centre, after the church, city hall, library, parish centre and office building.
facts.quote: The center consists of six buildings: Lakeuden Risti Church (1960) City Hall (1962) Municipal–Provincial Library (1965) Parish Center (1966) City and State Office Building (1968) City Theatre (1987)

facts.fact: The Aalto Centre is the administrative and cultural centre of Seinäjoki.
facts.quote: Aalto Center (Finnish: Aaltokeskus) is the administrative and cultural center of the City of Seinäjoki, Finland.

facts.fact: Finland's National Board of Antiquities lists the centre as a nationally significant built heritage site, and Docomomo has selected it as a significant example of modern architecture.
facts.quote: The National Board of Antiquities has listed the center as a nationally significant built heritage site. Docomomo has also selected it as a significant example of modern architecture in Finland.

facts.fact: In July 2026 the Aalto Centre was named a UNESCO World Heritage Site with 12 other Aalto works.
facts.quote: In July 2026, the Aalto Center, along with 12 other Aalto Works, was designated by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site.

facts.fact: Frank Lloyd Wright designed the house in 1959 in an organic style; it was his last residential design and was completed in 1967 by his former apprentice John Rattenbury of Taliesin Associated Architects.
facts.quote: Designed in 1959 by the architect Frank Lloyd Wright in an organic style, the two-story house was his last residential design, and was completed in 1967 by his onetime apprentice John Rattenbury of Taliesin Associated Architects.

facts.fact: Wright chose the site because it overlooks Palm Canyon and based his sketches on the location.
facts.quote: Wright selected the site because of its location overlooking Palm Canyon, designing sketches based on the location.

facts.fact: Seen from above, the plan is several overlapping circles drawn around five geometric centres, with a curving wing splitting off the circular main house.
facts.quote: The general plan, as seen from overhead, consists of several overlapping circles, which were drawn around five distinct geometric centers. A curving wing splits off the circular main section of the house.

facts.fact: It is one of 14 circular houses Wright designed, and one of six he designed around Phoenix.
facts.quote: It is one of 14 circular residences that Wright designed, as well as one of six that he designed around Phoenix.

facts.fact: The house is built mainly of rose-tinted concrete, and its windows face south towards Downtown Phoenix.
facts.quote: The structure is made primarily of rose-tinted concrete. Unlike Wright's other designs, which tended to face inward or away from crowded areas, the building's windows face Downtown Phoenix to the south.

facts.fact: Ledges above the windows keep strong sunlight from heating the interior.
facts.quote: The windows are topped by ledges to prevent large amounts of sunlight from heating up the house's interior, and there is a glass wall facing the patio and pool area.

facts.fact: A low-ceilinged foyer leads into larger rooms, an example of Wright's compression-and-release principle.
facts.quote: The Lykes House has a low-ceilinged foyer leading to larger rooms, an example of Wright's compression-and-release principle.

facts.fact: Unlike many Wright buildings, the house is not listed on the National Register of Historic Places.
facts.quote: In contrast to many of Wright's other designs, which are protected as official landmarks, the house is not listed on the National Register of Historic Places.

facts.fact: The functionalist villa of Dr. Viktor Bauer in Hrušovany u Brna was built in 1913–1914 by Adolf Loos and is a protected cultural monument.
facts.quote: There are two protected cultural monuments in the municipality. An architecturally valuable building is the functionalist villa of Dr. Viktor Bauer. It was built in 1913–1914 by the architect Adolf Loos.

facts.fact: Hrušovany u Brna lies about 16 km south of Brno, in the Dyje–Svratka Valley.
facts.quote: Hrušovany u Brna is located about 16 kilometres (10 mi) south of Brno. It lies in the Dyje–Svratka Valley.

facts.fact: Adolf Loos's Scheu House in Vienna (1913) was the childhood home of the modernist Elizabeth Close, née Scheu.
facts.quote: 1913 Scheu House, Vienna (childhood home of modernist Elizabeth Close, née Scheu)

facts.fact: The Jonson Gallery, on the University of New Mexico campus, was completed in 1950 as a combined home and gallery for the modernist painter Raymond Jonson.
facts.quote: The Jonson Gallery is a historic building on the campus of the University of New Mexico in Albuquerque, New Mexico, which was completed in 1950 as a combination home and gallery for the modernist painter Raymond Jonson.

facts.fact: It is a fairly sparse Pueblo Revival building by John Gaw Meem, who designed several other buildings on the campus.
facts.quote: The Jonson Gallery is a relatively sparse Pueblo Revival style building designed by John Gaw Meem, who also designed several other buildings on the university campus.

facts.fact: Set on a hillside, it has one storey above ground at the front and two at the back.
facts.quote: It sits on a hillside with one story above grade in the front and two in the back.

facts.fact: Steel casement windows with concrete sills are used throughout.
facts.quote: Steel casement windows with concrete sills are used throughout.

facts.fact: Jonson lived on the upper floor, and the gallery was on the lower floor.
facts.quote: The upper floor housed Jonson's residence, while the gallery space was on the lower floor.

facts.fact: The gallery was a centre for modern and abstract art in New Mexico; in 2009 its collections went to the University of New Mexico Art Museum and the building became offices.
facts.quote: During Jonson's lifetime and afterwards, the gallery was a center for modern and abstract art in New Mexico, as well as housing a large collection of Jonson's own works. In 2009, the gallery's collections were absorbed into the University of New Mexico Art Museum and the former gallery building was converted to office space.

facts.fact: The banker Franz Urbig commissioned the villa in 1915 on the shore of the Griebnitzsee at Babelsberg, just outside Potsdam.
facts.quote: In 1915 Franz Urbig commissioned the building of a family villa on the shores of the Griebnitzsee (lake) at Babelsberg, just outside Potsdam.

facts.fact: Its architect, Ludwig Mies van der Rohe, was little known at the time and later became a pioneer of modernism.
facts.quote: The architect, Ludwig Mies van der Rohe was little known at the time, though he would later - after radically changing his approach - achieve notability as a pioneer of modernist architecture,  becoming in 1930 the last director of the Bauhaus School in (since relocating from Weimar in 1925) Dessau.

facts.fact: The villa was built between 1915 and 1917.
facts.quote: The Villa Urbig was constructed between 1915 and 1917.

facts.fact: In July 1945 Winston Churchill stayed in the villa while attending the Potsdam Conference.
facts.quote: Between 16 July and 25 July 1945 the Villa Ubrig was briefly home to Winston Churchill, who was attending the Potsdam Conference nearby.

facts.fact: In East German times it served as a guest house for the 'Walter Ulbricht' academy for political and legal studies.
facts.quote: It was used for many years as a guest house for the "Walter Ulbricht" [East] German Academy for political and legal studies ("Deutsche Akademie für Staats- und Rechtswissenschaft "Walter Ulbricht" ").

facts.fact: After 1990 it returned to private ownership, and in 2005 Theodor Semmelhaack bought it and restored it comprehensively.
facts.quote: Following 1990 the Villa Urbig reverted to private ownership.   In 2005 it was acquired by Theodor Semmelhaack, a successful businessman and property developer who comprehensively restored it.

facts.fact: Carlo Mollino's Palazzo degli Affari in Turin, the Chamber of Commerce, dates from 1964–73 and still stands.
facts.quote: Camera di Commercio / Palazzo degli Affari (transl. Chamber of Commerce, 1964–73, Turin, extant)

facts.fact: Marcel Breuer designed Stillman House I in Litchfield, Connecticut, in 1950.
facts.quote: Stillman House I was designed by Marcel Breuer in Litchfield, Connecticut, United States, in 1950.

facts.fact: It follows Breuer's 'House in the Museum Garden', built the year before for the Museum of Modern Art.
